leverage.exposure: No leveraged position, and none is being opened. The balance is unchanged for the fifth run running, which confirms again that placing an offer does not debit anything until it clears. Both live bids have been sized so that the balance stays positive in every resolution order — the Frankfurt listing resolves in the morning, the Leipzig one in the afternoon, and neither sequence takes the account negative. This is the single number that must not be got wrong before the lock, so it bears repeating: do not raise either bid past the stated ceiling without selling a player first, and at the current squad size there is nobody who can be sold.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is no longer the squad shape — it is cash. With the Gomis bid committed there is a hard ceiling on any second offer, and that ceiling, not any view about the player, is what sets the Amaimouni bid. It sits in the low cluster while the listing type calls for the high one. The squad's own gap is the attacking third and the third midfield slot, and both are addressed by the two bids now in flight: Gomis fills the attack and unlocks the four-defender shape, Amaimouni replaces the only player in the eleven yet to score anything.

verdict.detail: The German transfer window shut at six this evening and took nobody out of the squad — the transfer-risk clause that has hung over every run since the weekend is now dead, and the eleven that finished the last run is the eleven that will face matchday two. That clears the way for the only decision on the table: one new buy, Ayoube Amaimouni of Eintracht Frankfurt, listed by Kickbase at exactly his market value half an hour before this run. He is a fit, confirmed starter — two starts from two, a full eighty-seven minutes on matchday one — and he is the best points-per-euro on this board after the Gomis bid already in flight. The catch is that the price is set by the bank, not by judgement: with the Gomis money committed there is only so much headroom left, and a bid capped at that headroom sits well below where contested Kickbase listings have actually been clearing. So the honest expectation is that this bid loses. Place it anyway — a losing bid costs nothing, because Kickbase does not debit until a bid clears, and the alternative is cash sitting idle scoring zero. Do not go a euro above the ceiling: both bids clearing on top of an over-sized offer would open a negative balance, and a negative balance at matchday start scores nothing for the entire matchday.

sell.reason: Nothing to sell, and that is a structural verdict rather than a judgement about any individual. At eleven players with one legal formation, every man in the squad is load-bearing: selling any of them drops the squad to ten, fills no formation at all, and hands over the hundred-point penalty by Georg's own hand — which is worth far more than anything the sale would bank. The three standing hold calls all remain in force for exactly this reason. Lokonga is still the worst value in the squad and is still bleeding market value, and Widmer is still a confirmed non-starter; both would be sold in a heartbeat if there were bodies to spare. There are not. The earliest any sale becomes possible is after the squad reaches thirteen, which would require both live bids to clear.

buy.reason: Amaimouni is the buy, and the case is unusually clean on the football and unusually constrained on the money. Frankfurt's number ten started matchday one at Union Berlin, played virtually the whole game, covered more ground than anyone else on this shortlist and won ten tackles; Ligainsider marks him fit, gives him two starts from two at eighty-six percent usage, and does not carry him on the injured-and-suspended table. The one cautionary item — a late-August note about competition for his position — is dated five days before he started, so the evidence runs the right way. He is a midfielder, which is where the squad is thinnest behind Nusa. Against him: he is listed by Kickbase rather than by a rival manager, and Kickbase listings in this league clear high, not near the asking price. A rival paid an eighteen percent premium for a goalkeeper on this same board barely an hour before this run. The bid being recommended is nowhere near that, because it cannot be — it is the largest number that keeps the balance positive whichever bid resolves first. Everything else on the board was checked and rejected. The newest listing, a defender put up half an hour ago, is the worst points-per-euro on the board by a wide margin and could not enter the eleven anyway with defence already full. The cheap Augsburg midfielder that looks superficially like the same bargain is the cameo-minutes trap: his season average was banked in ten and a half minutes of a game already won. Two manager asks re-checked this run — a Freiburg midfielder and a Hoffenheim defender — both fail on price and on shape at once.

That is PLUS 176 ap on the fielded eleven for one purchase - by far the largest single-move gain available, because a 0-scorer leaves the XI and a 176-scorer enters it. movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. There is not a single manager ask below market value anywhere on the board, so the mechanism a flip depends on is simply absent — and the evidence says the rivals have noticed too. Two separate managers tried to sell at or below a zero premium in the last day and found no buyer at all; one of them gave up this afternoon and sold his defender straight back to Kickbase at exactly market value. Money in this league is flowing to the board, not between managers. The micro-flips the rivals keep running on injured players remain motion rather than points and are still not a model to copy.

fitness.sweep: One flag, and it deserves attention without deserving panic. Kickbase has Bernardo carrying a status flag with the note that he did not come through the Cologne away game unscathed — the only non-zero status anywhere in the squad, and the first time this ledger has recorded it. The news does not agree. His Ligainsider profile marks him fit and its most recent dated item has him returning for that very Cologne game; Hoffenheim's entry on the injured-and-suspended table is completely empty. There is also a widely-circulated club post saying he is out injured — that one is for a Bayern fixture and therefore last season, since Hoffenheim host Dortmund on matchday two, and it must not be cited as evidence. What this costs is points, not the penalty: a flagged player still fills his slot in a legal formation. The mitigation is a formation change rather than a sale, and it only becomes available once the squad reaches twelve. Everyone else in the eleven is clean. Off the board, Frankfurt are carrying three absentees and none of them is the player being recommended.
